opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jesse Stewart (employee ID E013) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E013.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: admin
  - comment: Jesse Stewart (E013) is a full-time Payroll Specialist, and the Payroll Specialist role owns the Payroll system. Admin access is permitted for this employee, so I recommend granting admin to Payroll as requested.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E013 is a contractor with basic security training (HR note listed full_time; flagging discrepancy). Contractors with basic training max out at read, never admin. Requested admin exceeds maximum, so recommend read for Payroll.
reason: There is a discrepancy between the HR and Security notes about E013's employment type. HR lists full_time, but the Security agent looked up their own database and reports contractor with basic security training, flagging the discrepancy. Under policy, contractors with basic training max out at read and can never be admin. The requested admin exceeds the maximum, so the maximum (read) is granted. (If the HR note were correct, admin would be permitted, but I rely on the Security DB's directly-verified employment type and its explicit flag.)
